why: Every outbound call made on the instrument's own account, in every phase, declared before it is made. Schema /2 (attempt 4, 2026-09-21) adds `phase` and the `provision` section, because /1 said 'every outbound call the harness makes' while five fetches went around it entirely -- the image build's four installers and tarballs, and the model download -- which was a completeness claim true of the Python runtime and false of the pod. Phases: `provision` is fetched at IMAGE BUILD time and frozen by the image digest every manifest pins; `model_fetch` is the one thing a pod downloads at boot; `run` is the calls the harness itself makes through mark_platform.permitted_calls.call(), the only door, which refuses an id that is not declared here before a socket opens. The run's own components on loopback (mock world, model proxy, egress proxy, gateway, collector) are not calls out of the run and are not listed. `verified` states what each fetch is checked against, and says `distribution signatures, versions not pinned` or `none` where that is the truth -- 'pinned to a version' and 'verified by hash' are different facts and this document says which.

provision.where: packages/platform/pod/Dockerfile, built by .github/workflows/platform-image.yml on a linux/amd64 runner
provision.frozen_by: the image digest in packages/platform/pod/IMAGE, recorded as pins.image_digest in every run manifest
provision.boot_time_fetches: none: pod/setup.sh installs no tool and stops, naming the expected image, if one is absent
provision.history: until 2026-09-21 this build fetched node and uv by piping unpinned installers into a shell and extracted the otelcol and tempo tarballs unverified, from a base named by a floating tag. Every bundle published in attempts 1-3 cites a digest built that way: the bytes are frozen and reproducible, the inputs were never verified against their publishers.

fetches.verified: digest (was the tag 1.0.2-cu1281-torch280-ubuntu2404, which can move)

fetches.what: git curl ca-certificates bubblewrap firejail postgresql iptables sudo jq xz-utils procps ninja-build libcap2-bin util-linux

fetches.verified: a sha256 recorded in the Dockerfile, read 2026-09-21 from the project's published cosign_checksums.txt. THE FLOOR OF THE CHAIN: that file is attested by a sigstore bundle which needs cosign to verify, so verification bottoms out at one hash a person recorded.

cosign signature over the artifact, against a pinned identity (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/.github/workflows/base-release.yaml@refs/tags/v0.128.0) and issuer (https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com). This release publishes no .sha256 for the linux tarball; pinning the identity is what makes it a verification rather than 'signed by someone'.

calls.purpose: the pinned model files, the one thing a pod downloads at boot
calls.routed_note: made by huggingface_hub.snapshot_download in pod/model.sh, not through call(); declared so the inventory is complete
calls.verified: every file against benchmarks/model-pins/<repo>-<rev>.sha256, whose own sha256 is pins.model.hash in every manifest; the run refuses if one differs

calls.purpose: IMDSv2 session token so the identity document can be read
calls.read_only_basis: the token is a capability to read metadata for this instance, nothing on the provider changes

calls.purpose: the provider's statement of account, region and instance id
the provider's signature over the identity document, verified offline against the vendored regional certificate
the instance role's temporary credentials, used only to sign GetCallerIdentity; never written anywhere
the account and caller ARN the provider says these credentials belong to; corroborates the document's account id
calls.read_only_basis: GetCallerIdentity is documented by AWS as having no side effects and needing no permission

calls.purpose: the served model's id and metadata for the serving record
the serving engine's version for the serving record
the concurrency in effect at the model server, sampled through the run
spans exported to the collector by the OpenTelemetry SDK
calls.read_only_basis: the collector is the run's own instrument; the export writes the run's own spans to it and nothing outside the run
calls.routed_note: made by the SDK's exporter, not through call(); declared so the inventory is complete, counted from the exporter's own statistics
